plain.text: Pharaoh's cupbearer and chief baker offended him and were put in the prison where Joseph was. One night each had a dream. In the morning Joseph saw they were troubled and asked why. They said no one could interpret their dreams. Joseph said, "Don't interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams." The cupbearer dreamed of a vine with three branches whose grapes he squeezed into Pharaoh's cup. Joseph said that within three days Pharaoh would restore him to his position. "When all goes well with you, remember me and mention me to Pharaoh, and get me out of this prison. I was forcibly carried off from the land of the Hebrews, and even here I have done nothing to deserve being put in a dungeon." The baker dreamed of three baskets of bread on his head, with birds eating from the top one. Joseph said that within three days Pharaoh would hang him. Three days later, on Pharaoh's birthday, it happened just as Joseph had said. But the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph; he forgot him.

summary.bigIdea: Joseph interprets two prisoners' dreams through God's help, but the man he helped forgets him.
points: Joseph says interpretations belong to God.
The cupbearer is restored and the baker is executed, as Joseph said.
The cupbearer forgets Joseph, who stays in prison.
summary.reflection: Joseph was forgotten by someone he helped. How do you keep trusting God when people forget you?
